body:
FIXED. The masked-attention CPU kernel had an F32 arm guarded on the QUERY dtype alone and an F64 arm guarded on nothing. A mixed set — an F32 query against an F64 additive mask, which is what a trainable relative-position bias produces — matched the first guard and panicked reading the mask, or fell past it and panicked reading the query. The F32 arm now requires every tensor it reads to be F32, and the F64 fallthrough checks the same and hands anything mixed to the reference kernel, which reads through the dtype-agnostic accessor and is where this op went before the CPU kernel existed.

HOW IT REACHED MAIN: the only test exercising the shape trains a model and is skipped under -short, the lane CI runs. It had been panicking on the full suite. Found incidentally while benchmarking an unrelated llamagpu function whose test drives this path.

GATE: TestMHAMaskedMixedDtypeDoesNotPanic covers both mixings and asserts the result matches the reference kernel bit for bit, not merely that nothing panics. Restoring either the query-only guard or the missing delegation reddens it.

CHECK DRAFTED AND WITHHELD. PS3034 dtype-guard-misses-an-operand caught its motivating site exactly (4 findings pre-fix, 0 after) but reported 126 tree-wide, and the first sampled findings were all false. Two distinct noise sources, both diagnosed: (1) the dtype constraint is frequently SPLIT between an enclosing switch on one tensor dtype and an inner if on another, and a predicate reading only the if condition sees half the guard; (2) OUTPUT tensors are routinely allocated with the input dtype, so reading them as that dtype is guaranteed by construction rather than by the guard. A sound version needs to treat an enclosing type switch as part of the guard and to recognize outputs allocated from an input dtype. Recorded so a later attempt starts from the diagnosis.

RELATED: PS3027 is the same mistake on the OUTPUT side and did ship, because there the predicate is narrow — an INPUT view helper applied to a locally allocated output — with no equivalent noise.

Shipped M2 arm64 SIMD acceleration for the three F32 softmax row primitives: rowMax now uses 16-lane FMAXNM accumulation, scale uses 16-lane FMUL, and axpb uses 16-lane FMLA, each with scalar tails. rowMax repairs signed zero by selecting the first zero when the numeric maximum is zero, preserving ordered scalar semantics while still skipping NaNs. Non-arm64 SIMD targets and F64 behavior remain unchanged. Three paired count-7 M2 campaigns across 32x2048, 1x32000, 4x32000, 512x512, and 2048x2048 produced complete-operation median speedups of 1.507x to 2.493x and time reductions of 33.64% to 59.88%; 14 of 15 comparisons had p=.001 and one had p=.007. Cross-entropy forward improved 2.543x with 60.67% less time and backward improved 1.944x with 48.56% less time, both p=.001. MHA timings were statistically unchanged at p=.383 to .710 because the measured cases remain GEMM dominated. Tests cover finite and nonfinite values, tails, signed zeros, input immutability, and bit-exact parity for all three primitives. Disassembly confirms FMAXNM, FMUL, and FMLA. Benchmark evidence is recorded as M-01M0HFYEH0EKT, M-01M0HFZ7SAE1N, M-01M0HFZBW9FM4, and M-01M0HGM2TPENZ. Generalizable architecture-skew and partially vectorized pipeline detection was reported in jxsl13/perfscan#791. Durable signed-zero behavior is captured by SIMD-MAXNUM-PRESERVES-FIRST-ZERO-001.

note: targets revised

txt: WHEN an F32 MHA forward band is scheduled on arm64 under goexperiment.simd, the CPU backend SHALL use a band-row count divisible by 4 so every complete band feeds only whole rows into the four-row NEON GEMM tile.

WHEN three paired count-seven physical Apple M2 Pro campaigns measure causal MHA512 plus seq128 and seq512 full and GQA forward cells, the MHA band selector SHALL retain the selected band only if every causal MHA512 median is at least 1.15x faster than control 30 and no forward control has a statistically significant regression.

WHEN the selected ARM64 band schedule executes deterministic causal, full, and GQA F32 fixtures, the CPU backend SHALL preserve the exact control output digest and satisfy CPU-002 relative 2e-3 and absolute 1e-4 parity.

WHEN the build is not arm64 with goexperiment.simd or the MHA route is F64, backward, or query length below 16, the CPU backend SHALL preserve the existing 30-row non-target constant and prior route without selecting the ARM64 band override.

WHEN a 5 second MHA512 forward CPU profile is captured after promotion, the ARM64 MHA implementation SHALL make gemmF32RowsScalar flat samples no more than 5 percent of gemmF32Tile4x16Neon flat samples while adding zero steady-state allocations.
WHEN three paired count-seven M2 campaigns measure causal MHA512, the MHA band selector SHALL retain the selected band only if every median is at least 1.15x faster than control 30.
